idiom_name: case class document + circe Encoder/Decoder derivation
implementation_notes: A document is a case class (or a sealed trait hierarchy) and circe supplies the codecs: deriveEncoder/deriveDecoder, or the generic auto/semiauto imports, generate Encoder/Decoder instances, and io.circe.parser.parse plus decodeJson turns bytes into a typed document; circe-core itself ships no JSON parser, so parsing comes from the jawn subproject or the parser module, with circe-jackson available when Jackson should do it. Upickle and play-json are the other mainstream routes, and Scala 3 uses given/derives where Scala 2 used implicits, so derivation style is a floor decision. The case class is the document, the derived codec is the marshaller, and the endpoint pattern-matches on the decoded value to decide what to do - no message class required.
code_sketch:
case class OrderShipped(version: Int, orderId: String, lines: List[Line])

object OrderShipped:
  given Encoder[OrderShipped] = deriveEncoder
  given Decoder[OrderShipped] = deriveDecoder

val wire = OrderShipped(...).asJson.noSpaces                  // producer
parse(wire).flatMap(_.as[OrderShipped]) match                // receiver decides
  case Right(doc) => handle(doc)
  case Left(err)  => deadLetter(wire, err.getMessage)
pitfalls: Derived decoders ignore extra fields, so producer-side additions are tolerated but invisible; a misspelled mandatory field surfaces only as a missing-field error.
Automatic derivation through macros increases compile time sharply and leaks into type-inference errors; use semiautomatic derivation at module boundaries.
Scala 2 and Scala 3 derivation syntax (implicit versus given/derives) is not interchangeable, and libraries compiled for one cannot be mixed freely with the other.
Derivation works from member names, so renaming a case class field silently changes the wire format unless wire names are pinned explicitly before the first message ships.
